description: Assertions for tools/repro-eval.js. must_fire proves the auditor still catches a defect; must_not_fire proves it has not become permissive; min_producers / min_checks are the floors that prove it still parses anything at all. A repro-audit that reads zero sidecars reports zero defects, which is indistinguishable from a fully gated repo — that ambiguity is the failure mode these floors exist to close.

cases.name: gated-ok
cases.why: The shape the discipline produces: a producer that reproduced its shipped number within its declared tolerance, with a pin that still resolves to the value its cited source carries. Nothing should fire.

cases.name: ungated
cases.why: The headline finding. A producer emitting four new numerics with no gate block reproduced nothing before reporting them, and every downstream audit will still pass because the prose quotes those numerics faithfully.

cases.name: gate-failed
cases.why: A gate that claims status ok while its own delta exceeds its own declared tolerance. The self-reported status is not the check — recomputing |delta| against the tolerance is.

cases.name: stale-pin
cases.why: The quiet one. The gate passes forever because the pin is a literal, but the shipped number moved upstream (0.691 to 0.680), so the producer now certifies itself against a retired value. Citing source + source_path is what makes this visible.

cases.name: skipped
cases.why: A skip is legitimate when a stream genuinely has no shipped number (a rate-thinned cache), and is an escape hatch otherwise. The reason string is the whole difference, so an undocumented skip has to fire and a documented one has to not.

cases.name: uncited
cases.why: A passing gate whose shipped value is a bare literal. It is not wrong today, but nothing can tell whether it is still current, so it degrades into a stale pin without ever changing state.

cases.name: empty
cases.why: The fixture this tool exists to trip. No sidecars means nothing was checked, and a tool that prints a clean report here is the exact silent-auditor failure the notebook corpus was built to catch. Must exit nonzero.

cases.name: python-dialect
cases.why: json.dump emits bare NaN / Infinity / -Infinity, which JSON.parse rejects. On the attentional-foraging output tree a strict reader failed on most sidecars and therefore saw none of the gates inside them: a parse error reads as a broken file, not as an auditor that has gone blind. Adjacent NaNs in one array share a delimiter, which is why the substitution runs twice.

cases.name: whole-corpus
cases.why: Walked as one tree, the auditor has to still separate the gated producer from the six defective ones. A recursive walk that collapses them, or one that stops at the first directory, shows up here and not in the single-case runs.
